input.question: Why is it that when I'm really drunk I can barely taste what I'm drinking, but I feel like I'm hypersensitive to how food tastes?
input.ground_truth: Because you are becoming taste blind to the beer over time. If you sit in a room that has a nice smell you'll eventually not be able to smell it over time. Same thing applies if you drink Keystone all night (the fact that it has a mild taste and makes you intoxicated only amplifies the effect) but if you eat something that is very flavorful then it makes a greater impression.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why is it that when I'm really drunk I can barely taste what I'm drinking, but I feel like I'm hypersensitive to how food tastes?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your tongue is like a little TV that tells your brain what you’re tasting. When you drink a lot of alcohol, the “TV” gets fuzzy and doesn’t work very well, so you can’t taste your drink very well.

But when you eat food, your mouth and nose work together to help you taste. Alcohol can make your nose stuffy, but sometimes it makes you notice flavors in food even more, like how everything seems extra yummy or spicy. It’s kind of like when you have a stuffy nose and then you take a bite of something and it tastes super strong!

So, when you’re really drunk, drinks taste weird or not very strong, but food can taste super strong or even funny because your brain is paying more attention to it.
